name: Tres leches cake
origin: Pastel de tres leches, popular across Mexico and Central America; a light sponge baked first, then soaked after baking in a mixture of evaporated milk, sweetened condensed milk and cream, the three milks the cake is named for.

process.name: whip eggs and sugar
process.description: whip whole eggs with sugar to a light, pale foam

process.name: fold in flour and butter
process.description: fold in sifted flour and leavening, then a small amount of melted butter

process.name: soak
process.description: once cooled, pierce and soak the sponge in a mixture of evaporated milk, sweetened condensed milk and cream until fully absorbed

notes: The base is a standard light egg-foam sponge, close to genoise.json's own proportion, chosen for its real ability to absorb a large volume of milk without collapsing. The three-milk soak that gives the cake its name and character is a real, post-bake process step (using cow-milk-whole and cream from the substance registry, plus a sweetened condensed milk this catalogue's registry does not yet carry), deliberately kept out of the baker's-percentage ingredient list: that list describes one mixed batter, and a soak applied to an already-set, already-baked crumb is a different physical process (diffusion into a porous solid, not a batter setting), not a second batter ingredient.
